ann_36.text: This part acts on 117 of 242 training patients (48%), who have more ST depression on exercise than the rest; 77 of them had heart disease.
For them it clearly raises the risk (odds about 1.4 times on average, on the model's odds scale).
ST depression adds to the risk through this part only once it rises above about 0.9 mm.
ST depression raises the risk, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect (from 0 to 2.8 mm, odds about ×6.2 against ×2.7 with a normal scan, on the model's odds scale).
It also raises the risk more if the resting ECG is normal than if it shows left ventricular hypertrophy.

ann_38.text: This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.4 percentage points of risk).

ann_39.text: This part acts on 203 of 242 training patients (84%); they tend to be older and to have more ST depression on exercise than the rest.
For them it clearly raises the risk (odds about 1.4 times on average, on the model's odds scale), and 102 of the 203 had heart disease.
Through it, ST depression on exercise adds to the risk only once it rises above about 1.3 mm.
ST depression raises the risk, and even more so if resting blood pressure is 130 mm Hg or lower.
Age adds to the risk through this part only once it passes about 53 years, and only slightly.
A reversible defect on the thallium scan raises the risk slightly here, and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG lower it slightly.

ann_40.text: The model gives the biggest increase in risk to patients with more major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy: from 0 to 2 vessels, the odds rise about 30 times on average, on the model's odds scale.
Compared with patients who have no chest pain symptoms, it gives a much lower risk to patients with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain, and a lower risk to patients with atypical angina.
Women get a clearly lower risk than men (odds about 0.10 times those of men, on the model's odds scale).

A flat ST segment at peak exercise, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm), higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL), a reversible defect on the thallium scan, higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg), chest pain brought on by exercise and older age each clearly raise the risk.
A higher maximum heart rate and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL clearly lower the risk.

For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk 19%), the largest changes on the model's odds scale are about ×30 for 2 vessels instead of 0, about ×6 for a flat instead of an upsloping ST segment and about ×0.1 for a woman instead of a man.

The model has little data on a fixed defect on the thallium scan (15 patients, lower risk), a downsloping ST segment (17 patients, slightly higher risk) and a thallium result coded 4 (2 patients, higher risk; the code is not defined).

ann_36.original: Hidden gate 204 = ReLU(2.554*oldpeak + 1.133*thal:7 + 0.937*restecg:0 + 0.276): a one-sided ischaemia-evidence detector that switches on for patients with exercise-induced ST depression and/or a reversible thallium defect, normal resting ECG adding a little. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): hard-zero for 52%, active for 48%; mean |grad| oldpeak 1.23 > thal:7 0.55 > restecg:0 0.45; oldpeak alone correlates 0.88 with the gate. This is the output-facing copy 204_a (bit-identical to 204_b); it reads out directly to the output with +0.117, raising predicted risk.
ann_36.proposed: A part that raises the risk once ST depression on exercise exceeds about 0.9 mm, more so with a reversible thallium defect or a normal resting ECG.

ann_38.original: Serial chain thal:6 -> 3671 -> 2116: 3671 = ReLU(1.000*thal:6 + 2.123), 2116 = ReLU(1.003*3671 + 0.036). Since thal:6 >= -0.257 on the data both ReLUs are always active (100% on train), so 2116 = 1.003*thal:6 + 2.165 exactly (r = 1.000 on train). It feeds gate 290 with weight -0.013, contributing -0.013*thal:6 - 0.029 to its pre-activation: an always-on affine relay that is functionally a vestige.
ann_38.proposed: This part barely changes the predictions.

ann_39.original: Serial composition of the ischaemia gate into a BP-adjusted gate and its readouts. (1) Gate 290 = ReLU(1.088*st_ischaemia_gate_bp - 0.817*trestbps + 0.151*cp:2 + 0.017*cp:3 + 0.046*thal:6 - 0.013*thal6_linear_passthrough - 0.485): it passes on the ischaemia evidence of 204_b, offset downward by resting blood pressure (high-BP patients need more ST-depression evidence to open it). (2) 1834 = ReLU(0.941*290 - 1.672): high-threshold amplifier, fires only when 290 > 1.78, making the pathway convex. (3) 1987 = ReLU(0.880*age - 1.585*290 + 0.179): an age term switched OFF by the gate, so age adds risk only for patients in whom 290 is quiet. Output contribution 0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 290 active 56% (100/135 of its active cases have 204 on; 35 open from low BP alone, mean predicted risk 0.13); 1834 active 26%, only when 204 and 290 are both on, and 78% of those patients are diseased; 1987 active in 64% of patients with 290 quiet vs 13% with 290 active. Interpretation: the network has exactly one nonlinear mechanism - an ischaemia pathway that amplifies strong ST-depression/defect evidence and uses age as a fallback signal when that evidence is absent.
ann_39.proposed: A part that acts on most patients and raises their risk: ST depression adds risk above about 1.3 mm, more so at lower resting blood pressure, and age adds a little above about 53 years.

ann_40.original: Root: logit z = -0.496 + LINEAR CORE + 0.117*st_ischaemia_gate_output + ischaemia_pathway readouts (0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987); prediction = sigmoid(z) (the genome output node is ReLU but the evaluator overrides it with sigmoid for binary classification, so it is a logistic score). ann_40.proposed: More vessels coloured by fluoroscopy, a flat ST segment, more ST depression on exercise, higher cholesterol, a reversible thallium defect and higher resting blood pressure raise the risk. Being a woman, typical or non-anginal chest pain rather than none and a higher maximum heart rate lower it.

summary.text: The model's strongest signal is the number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy: from 0 to 2 vessels the odds of heart disease rise about 30 times on average, on the model's odds scale.
Women, and patients with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain rather than no chest pain symptoms, get a clearly lower risk.
A flat ST segment at peak exercise, more ST depression on exercise, higher cholesterol, a reversible thallium defect and higher resting blood pressure each clearly raise the risk.
ST depression on exercise raises the risk, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect or the resting ECG is normal.
Through one part of the model, ST depression adds to the risk only once it rises above about 0.9 mm.

worth_checking.text: Worth checking: the model treats fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL as lowering the risk (odds about 0.45 times, on the model's odds scale).
Worth checking: patients with typical angina get the lowest risk of all chest pain types, below patients with no chest pain symptoms.
Worth checking: the model treats a fixed defect on the thallium scan as lowering the risk compared with a normal scan, from only 15 training patients.
Worth checking: one part adds more risk for ST depression when resting blood pressure is 130 mm Hg or lower than when it is higher.

ann_36.text: This part acts on 117 of 242 training patients (48%).
For them it clearly raises the risk of heart disease (odds about ×1.40 on average, on the model's odds scale).
In the training data, 77 of these 117 patients had heart disease.

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect (odds about ×6.2 for patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan against ×2.7 for patients with a normal thallium scan, on the model's odds scale).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal (odds about ×5.5 for patients with a normal resting ECG against ×2.4 for patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan a higher risk than patients with a normal thallium scan, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal (odds about ×3.3 for patients with a normal resting ECG against ×2.8 for patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, on the model's odds scale).
Through this part, ST depression on exercise only adds to the risk of heart disease once it rises above about 0.9 mm (73 training patients are past that point).

The model clearly treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease through this part: going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm changes the odds by about ×1.60 on average, on the model's odds scale.

Through this part, the model also slightly raises the risk of heart disease with a reversible defect on the thallium scan (rather than a normal thallium scan); it slightly lowers it with signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG).

ann_38.text: Through this part, the model also slightly lowers it with a fixed defect on the thallium scan (rather than a normal thallium scan).
This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.4 percentage points of risk).

ann_39.text: This part acts on 203 of 242 training patients (84%).
For them it clearly raises the risk of heart disease (odds about ×1.43 on average, on the model's odds scale).
In the training data, 102 of these 203 patients had heart disease.

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease, and even more so if resting blood pressure is at or below 130 mm Hg (odds about ×4.3 for patients with resting blood pressure at or below 130 mm Hg against ×2.9 for patients with resting blood pressure above 130 mm Hg, on the model's odds scale).
Through this part, ST depression on exercise only adds to the risk of heart disease once it rises above about 1.3 mm (71 training patients are past that point).
Through this part, age only adds to the risk of heart disease once it rises above about 53 years (85 training patients are past that point).

The model clearly treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease through this part: going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm changes the odds by about ×2.3 on average, on the model's odds scale.

Through this part, the model also slightly raises the risk of heart disease with a reversible defect on the thallium scan (rather than a normal thallium scan), a higher age, atypical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)), a fixed defect on the thallium scan (rather than a normal thallium scan) and non-anginal chest pain (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)); it slightly lowers it with signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG).

ann_40.text: The model clearly treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 0 vessels to 2 vessels changes the odds by about ×30 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model clearly gives patients with typical angina a lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms (asymptomatic) (odds about ×0.08 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives women a lower risk than men (odds about ×0.10 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients with a flat ST segment a higher risk than patients with an upsloping ST segment (odds about ×6.1 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients with non-anginal chest pain a lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms (asymptomatic) (odds about ×0.18 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm changes the odds by about ×3.6 on average, on the model's odds scale.

The model clearly treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) changes the odds by about ×3.6 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model clearly gives patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan a higher risk than patients with a normal thallium scan (odds about ×3.0 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly treats a higher resting blood pressure as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 110 mm Hg to 155 mm Hg changes the odds by about ×2.8 on average, on the model's odds scale.

The model gives patients with thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded) a higher risk than patients with a normal thallium scan (odds about ×2.4 on average, on the model's odds scale). The model has little data on this: only 2 training patients (thallium stress test result coded 4 (meaning not recorded)).

The model clearly gives patients with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL a lower risk than patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less (odds about ×0.45 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan a lower risk than patients with a normal thallium scan (odds about ×0.49 on average, on the model's odds scale). The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

The model clearly treats a higher maximum heart rate as lowering the risk of heart disease: going from 118 beats per minute to 175 beats per minute changes the odds by about ×0.53 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model clearly gives patients with atypical angina a lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms (asymptomatic) (odds about ×0.54 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise a higher risk than patients without chest pain on exercise (odds about ×1.81 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly treats a higher age as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 42 years to 66 years changes the odds by about ×1.44 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model also slightly raises the risk of heart disease with a downsloping ST segment (rather than an upsloping ST segment).

For a typical patient (the median training patient for every number and the most common category for the rest; predicted risk 19%), the odds change, on the model's odds scale, by about number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy from 0 vessels to 2 vessels: ×30; typical angina rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic): ×0.08; female rather than male: ×0.10; a flat ST segment rather than an upsloping ST segment: ×6.1; ST depression on exercise from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm: ×3.8.
